AGENTS.md

Source: AGENTS.md

Project purpose

This repository contains qgsim, an R package for specifying, validating, running, and comparing breeding-scheme simulations through a common R interface.

The package is intended as an orchestration layer for simulation tools implemented in R, C++, Fortran, Python, Julia, or other languages. It should not reimplement all simulators in R. Instead, it should provide a common specification, validation layer, backend contract, and standardized result format.

Repository type

This is an R package repository.

Typical content includes:

  • R/: R source code
  • tests/testthat/: package tests
  • man/: generated roxygen documentation
  • README.md / README.Rmd: package overview and examples
  • DESCRIPTION: package metadata and dependencies
  • NAMESPACE: generated by roxygen2
  • qgsim.Rproj: RStudio project file

General rules

  • Work only inside this repository.
  • Do not commit changes unless explicitly asked.
  • Check git status --short before editing.
  • If the working tree is dirty, identify existing changes before editing.
  • Do not overwrite unrelated user changes.
  • Prefer small, reviewable edits.
  • Show the diff after edits.
  • Do not delete files unless explicitly asked.
  • Do not push to GitHub unless explicitly asked.

R package rules

  • Preserve valid R package structure.
  • Do not edit NAMESPACE or man/ by hand unless explicitly asked.
  • Use roxygen comments for documentation updates.
  • Run devtools::document() only when documentation changes require it.
  • Keep exported API changes deliberate and documented.
  • Avoid adding new dependencies unless clearly justified.
  • If adding dependencies, update DESCRIPTION and explain why.
  • Prefer base R where practical.
  • Keep examples small and reproducible.

qgsim architecture rules

Preserve the explicit workflow:

breeding_scheme() -> qgsim_compile() -> qgsim_validate() -> qgsim_run() -> qgsim_result

Important design principles:

  • Separate specification from execution.
  • qgsim_run() should accept a compiled qgsim_plan.
  • Avoid overlapping orchestration APIs.
  • Keep qgsim_plan backend-neutral.
  • Do not add backend-specific fields to the common plan.
  • Validate individual descriptors and complete plans.
  • Keep backend contracts explicit and testable.
  • Standardize all backend outputs into qgsim_result.
  • Do not wrap unconstrained backend-native output as a public result.
  • Keep schema versions explicit.
  • Preserve deterministic behavior for seeded reference-backend tests.

Backend rules

Backends should follow the contract:

available()
translate()
execute()
collect()

Responsibilities:

  • available() checks whether the backend can run.
  • translate() converts a qgsim_plan to backend-native input.
  • execute() runs the backend.
  • collect() converts backend-native output into a valid qgsim_result.

Do not mix backend discovery, translation, execution, and result collection in one function.

For external C++/Fortran/Python/Julia tools:

  • Prefer file-based or JSON-based exchange formats.
  • Keep backend-specific artifacts referenced through result files/provenance.
  • Do not require external tools for core package tests.
  • Add backend contract tests before adding real external integrations.

Testing rules

Use the smallest relevant check for the change.

Common checks:

devtools::load_all()
devtools::test()

For focused tests:

testthat::test_file("tests/testthat/test-file-name.R")

For documentation changes:

devtools::document()

For the current minimal package, useful checks include:

Rscript -e "devtools::load_all(); testthat::test_dir('tests/testthat')"

Ask before running long checks or adding heavy external dependencies.

Simulation and scientific rules

  • The current r_reference backend is for validating architecture, not for scientific conclusions.
  • Do not describe the reference backend as a complete breeding-scheme simulator.
  • Do not invent simulation results, benchmarking claims, or biological interpretations.
  • Keep examples clearly labelled as minimal or illustrative.
  • Preserve reproducibility for seed-based tests.
  • Add scientific realism incrementally and with tests.

Documentation rules

  • README examples should run with the minimal installed package.
  • Clearly distinguish implemented features from planned backends.
  • Mention that external tool integration is future/extension work unless implemented.
  • Keep documentation concise and practical.

Preferred response style

When reporting back:

  • State what was inspected.
  • State what was changed.
  • List checks run.
  • Mention checks not run.
  • Highlight risks or follow-up work.
  • Keep recommendations concrete and actionable.
